design: Tier 2: a migration. HAZARD: 0121 recreates spec_documents to relax ck_spec_documents_kind_phase to (capability AND phase IN (current, archived)) OR (not capability AND phase != current); it reaches the operator's real :8000 database at their next restart, and the UI bundle reaches :8000's app at its next reload. Nothing existing changes value. Rollback: downgrade sets any archived capability back to current, then restores the narrow CHECK (retirements are lost; requirement rows stay retired until the next reindex). Decision (operator 2026-10-08: 'Build retire a capability'): reuse archived rather than a new phase, so the vocabulary and the index's statuses do not grow; the reason and absorbing capability live on the phase event, not a column. Requirements are retired by one rule in the index (archived capability => retired), not by editing the file, so the file stays the record. Folds into spec-document-authority.

checked: hub/hub/spec_lifecycle.py TRANSITIONS has no edge out of current
hub/hub/db/models.py ck_spec_documents_kind_phase ties capability to current
hub/hub/spec_index.py requirements_from_payload indexes every payload requirement as active

problem: F536: quiet-hours (a sample), trace-timeline (never built) and opencode-config (runner removed) describe nothing in the code, and two capabilities that overlap cannot be combined: DELETE refuses a capability (delete_capability), `current` has no transition, and a merge can only empty one, leaving an empty `current` capability in the map, the index and coverage.

requirements.rationale: A corpus that cannot lose a capability keeps describing features that do not exist. Open work against it must be decided first, or that work would serve requirements nobody holds any more.
requirements.statement: The operator MUST be able to move a capability from current to archived, stating a reason and optionally naming the current capability that absorbed it; the move MUST be refused without a reason, when the named capability is not another current capability, when the actor is not the operator, and while a task that is neither approved nor rejected links one of its active requirements.

requirements.rationale: Coverage, linking and evidence all read the requirement index; a retired capability's requirements must leave all three at once, and a reindex from the unchanged file must not bring them back.
requirements.statement: Every requirement of an archived capability MUST be retired when it is archived and MUST stay retired whenever the document is indexed again.

requirements.rationale: The file is the record of what the capability said when it was retired.
requirements.statement: A merge or fold into an archived capability MUST be refused, writing nothing.

requirements.rationale: Why a capability left, and where its behaviour went, must be readable later from the document's own history.
requirements.statement: Retiring MUST record a phase event carrying the reason and the absorbing capability, re-render the file with its archived status, and keep the document in spec/index.json with status archived.

requirements.rationale: Retiring is an operator decision made where the operator reads the capability.
requirements.statement: A current capability's view in the app MUST offer Retire, asking for the reason and optionally the absorbing capability, and MUST show the Hub's refusal when one is returned.

in_scope: A current -> archived edge for capability documents, operator-only, with a required reason and an optional absorbing capability
Retiring every requirement of a retired capability, and keeping them retired on any later reindex
Refusing a merge or fold into a retired capability
A Retire action on a capability in the app
non_goals: Deleting a capability or its file: the file and its history stay
Un-retiring: there is no transition out of archived, as for changes
Moving the requirements to the absorbing capability: that is a separate, authored merge
Retiring change, roadmap or system-map documents: they have their own archive rules

summary: The operator can retire a capability that no longer describes the product: with a stated reason, and optionally naming the capability that absorbed it. A retired capability is archived: its requirements are retired, so they leave coverage and nothing can link to them; no merge or fold can write to it; and its file stays as the record of what it said.
